details: Introduction to Rebirthing Breathwork and how it can be used as a tool to regulate the central nervous system
bio: Jessica is a Rebirthing Breathworker currently in her final year of study. She shares a gentle, self-led and self-paced style of breathwork that supports participants to reconnect with their inner world at their own pace. Her work weaves intention setting, nervous system education and emotional awareness, supporting people to understand the language of their body, meet big emotions with presence and explore the patterns that shape their relationships.

details: Tree Holding Qi Gong really captures that harmony between grounding and flow. The phrase “Stillness in Movement” is especially powerful—it reflects the deep presence and calm awareness cultivated in
bio:
Hi, my name is Jamie Josephs. I’m the lead instructor at the Ballarat School of Jik Cheung Kung Fu in Ballarat Central, Victoria. Over the last three decades I’ve immersed myself in Jik Cheung Kung Fu, Western boxing, Tai Chi, and internal arts, earning my Second Degree Black Belt along the way. My teaching focuses on practical self-defence, situational awareness, personal empowerment, and close-quarter skills for students aged 16 and over.

At festivals I love sharing Tree Holding Qigong — a gentle yet powerful practice that brings together breath, posture, balance, and meditation. It’s an invitation to root yourself like a tree, calm the mind, reconnect with your body, and discover stillness within movement. My sessions are all about helping people find presence, inner strength, and a sense of peace.

details: Building connection through Harmonising, resonating and chanting to Shruti box to build connection then into a small breath work with omm chants at the end leaving people filled with love 🥰
bio: I'm Ben, I'm 32 and I want to to grow and help people grow, I'm just stepping into the scene but I want to provide something special to people and to bring community and the feeling of togetherness back to people, I'm still learning but my intuition is leading me and I feel like it knows where I need to be and that's here 👌😌

details: I offer spiritual practices with simple explanations as to how they affect physiology. Using breathing/meditation/affirmations - I offer simple dally practices to help guide people home: to the self
bio:
Helen is a research scientist that has turned her hand to discovering more natural and holistic ways of healing. After working as a nutritionist for many years she learned that most people with an eating 'dis-order' are actually using food to conceal past trauma. Helen found that by shifting the focus from food to treating the underlying issues, she was much more successful at helping her clients change their eating behaviours.

Over the last 15 years Helen has been on a journey of self-discovery, delving into the healing power of meditation, breath, and nature. Coupled with her extensive scientific knowledge of nutrient interactions, and her holistic approach to treatment, she will introduce you a new way of living. One that is more in tune with your internal rhythm.

details: Deep Ecology and Ecosophia documentaries
bio: Documentary filmmaker

details: Drop in, rest, receive. You'll be guided in a simple meditation while receiving VortexHealing - Divine Energy Healing. Think Reiki on steroids, with specific focuses that the group needs.
bio: Chris has been studying energy healing modalities for over 30 years, and professional healer since 2012. In the last 6 years, VortexHealing has become his main practice with clients due to its potency, precision, and depth, and how it gracefully leads you into deeper states of awakening.

details: We’ll use Futures Studies to reflect on scenarios we (un)consciously hold & define our best paths into whatever happens. Bring your thinking caps, joy in sharing, & lets explore our futures!
bio: Chris (BComm/Psych; MsSc Strategic Foresight) spent a decade+ facilitating groups to explore their futures, including NGOs, government departments, corporates, and industry bodies. Chris helped establish the Melbourne Social Forum 2004, project managed the Davos connected National Futures Summit 2006-2007, Co-Chaired the Australasian Node of UN's Millennium Project 2009-2012, was COO of the Centre for Australian Foresight 2012-2015. He’s published in futures journals (eg Humanicide: A Risk Profile for Humanity in the 21st Century) and through the Australian Foresight Institute on topics like Government Institutes of Foresight, and futures of philanthropy and not-for-profit sectors.

details: A sound activation and music accompaniment using the sacred AUM offers deep meditation, supporting stress reduction, mental clarity, emotional release, nervous system balance and self-connection.
bio:
Nectar of Sounds is a fusion of handpan melodies and conscious soundscapes, designed to transport listeners into deep meditative states. Blending rhythmic flow with harmonic resonance, these sounds offers a sonic journey that soothes the mind, awakens the senses, and fosters inner stillness.

On a personal level, Ali is a dedicated sound bath facilitator with a deep-rooted understanding of the human system through the lens of yoga and wellness. After 5 years of preparation and in 2013, he completed an intensive six-month advanced Hatha Yoga Teacher Training program in India, encompassing over 1,750 hours of rigorous sadhana. His training provided a profound foundation in the mechanics of yogic postures, the impact of sound and vibrations on the body and mind, mantras, anatomy and physiology, diet, the ancient science of Siddha, yogic philosophy, lifestyle practices, and the influence of the five elements. He spent 12 years living in the ashram where he undertook his teacher training, fully immersing himself in a disciplined yogic lifestyle and deepening his experential knowledge. Since completing his training, he has been teaching and sharing his knowledge, guiding individuals on their journey towards their inner wellbeing. With this holistic knowledge and experiences, Ali curates immersive sound experiences that promote deep relaxation, balance, and inner harmony, guiding participants on a journey of profound well-being.

details: Inspired by Pleasure Activism, this is an embodiment practice for Women & Femmes to resource their nervous system through the healing benefits of Pleasure. "Make the revolution irresistible!"
bio:
Jordhana is an Embodied Counselling Practitioner, Somatic Sexologist and Health Behaviour Change Coach. She completed her training at the Institute of Somatic Sexology, and Wellcoaches School of Coaching (USA). Jordhana is a certified member of the Somatic Sex Educators Association of Australasia and the Health Coaches Association of Australia and New Zealand and she specialises in Health, Pleasure and Embodiment Coaching for Women. 

Jordhana's practice is informed by her background in Naturopathy and Yoga Teaching, having completed her Bachelor of Health Science (Naturopathy) at the Southern School of Natural Therapies, and an Advanced Diploma of Yoga Teaching through the Australian Institute of Yoga Therapy.

Jordhana is deeply inspired by the work of Adrienne Marree Brown’s 'Pleasure Activism'. She sees Pleasure as an essential force for change in the world, both personally and collectively, and seeks to “make the revolution irresistible”.

details: An invitation to slow down, sense inward, and trust the emergent wisdom of the body — a somatic enquiry into what you’re carrying and what’s quietly asking for your care.

details: Start the day with some self love.. Energise your body, clear your mind and feel the joy. Variations offered/ All levels.. especially those “terrible” at "yoga" (which no-one is, ever..)
bio:
I work in film and balance the madness with yoga. I had a school in Hepburn Springs and Melbs and love to share yoga in community cos it's more fun than on the mat at home alone. I offer yoga to a diverse bunch and recognise that we all need something different depending on age, experience, energy levels on the day and I encourage deep listening, responding and to lighten up a little (or a lot? ..about it all:) 
I love sharing yoga at festivals in nature and have done for decades.. x Lisa

details: This workshop provides an intro to non-duality spiritual teachings. We will explore how reality is a single undivided whole - there is no distinct and separate 'me' that stands apart from the world.
bio: Shanti is an experienced facilitator of meditation and qi gong workshops, and is the author of the book 'The Peaceful Place - The Amazingly Simple Guide to Finding Peace Within"

details: Moving meditation, facilitated by heartful music, to move your body however it wants to move ❤️
bio: Aeron has been dancing for decades, and several years ago, moved towards DJ'ing and facilitating ecstatic dance journeys. If the music has heart, soul, bass and beats, he's into it ❤️

details: Join this workshop to explore our shared understanding of Food systems and community, the effects of climate change and your place in it- community is how we adapt.
bio: Chelsea McNab - Executive Officer of Yarra Valley ECOSS (Community Environment Hub), member of Moora Moora Cooperative Community of 25 years, Sustainability Officer managing Food Systems and Food Security projects for Yarra Ranges Council, mother of 3, farmer and activist.

workshop_name: Shamanism, Power, and Politics: A Conversational Exploration
details: This workshop is an open, inquiry-based space to explore how shamanic practices have intersected with power, authority, and social order—both in traditional societies and in modern political contexts.
bio: Her interest in shamanism began at a very young age and has profoundly shaped her life. Through living with tribal communities, engaging with diverse shamanic traditions, and reconnecting with her ancestral heritage, she has developed a deep respect for this field. Passionate about learning and sharing, she offers a space for open dialogue where knowledge is exchanged freely. This space is not about right or wrong, but about shared experience and exploring a complex topic together.

details: Discover the sacred union within and the forces that shape your life. Unite your inner masculine and feminine through this embodied journey to awaken clarity, power, connection, and inner harmony.
bio:
Klaudia is a lifelong explorer, passionate dancer, and a curator of immersive experiences where people can deepen their connection with their body, energy, and soul. She has trained in a wide range of embodied practices, including tantra, shamanic healing, shadow work, authentic relating, emotional release, and tantric dance.

Tantra has been her path to growth and transformation — a way to cultivate love, presence, and joy, and bring greater consciousness to every area of life. Klaudia’s passion for embodiment comes from its power to reconnect us with our true essence, unlocking inner wisdom, expression, and freedom. Her mission is to support others in awakening their authentic selves, uncovering unconscious patterns, and experiencing deeper self-awareness, empowerment, and vitality.

Through her work, Klaudia creates powerful spaces where participants can feel, move, and explore their inner landscapes safely and deeply. In The Alchemy of Inner Union, she guides participants to explore the dynamic interplay of their inner masculine and feminine, helping them cultivate harmony, presence, and the transformative power of inner union. The workshop draws on classical tantric philosophy, inviting embodied exploration in a non-sexual space.

details: What does "elder" mean to you and "us"? A shared exploration of our felt-sense and needs around this. A space to reimagine and to let new meanings and relationships emerge.
bio: Aisha has worked professionally in the community space for 26 years. She is a somatic psychotherapist, relationship counsellor, social worker and community educator. Currently she specialises in sexual assault trauma, working at Victorian Aboriginal Health Service and CASA House for many years prior. Her lived journey is the deepest source of utter belief in an inherent human capacity for healing, beauty and wisdom. This imbues her practice approach with a continual deep sensing of the body, soul and the sacred. She is excited to explore and weave together with others at Evolve.

details: A playful exploration of humour’s role within human ecosystems and how comic versus tragic thinking influences behaviour, culture and environment.
bio:
I'm a comic, thinker, writer & speaker with a deep interest in the intelligence of humour and the art of comedy, not just as forms of entertainment, but as vital, inherent, creative capacities that shape how we perceive, narrate and adapt to our experience. 

I’d like to share some of the joy I’ve found in writing and performing stand-up comedy, explore connections between humour and nature, and dispel common myths that can inhibit people from sharing their unique sense of humour, with the wider world.

details: Let's come together and start co-creating communal safety in Evolve. What does communal safety mean? What does it provide? What does it prevent? What do we need? How do we get there?
bio: I’m a facilitator drawn to the "messy middle"—those undefined spaces where community wisdom is most needed. I’ve spent the last few years at ConFest contributing to the Emergency Management Team and advocating for better sexual safety. I see safety not as a set of rules, but as a living system we create together. I’m not here with the answers; I’m here to hold the space for us to discover what communal safety looks like for our unique Evolve container.

details: Where Ecstatic dance has a wave, Contact Improv has principles. Where Ecstatic dance focuses on self-inquiry and self-expression, Contact focuses on the body's mechanics and the mechanics of bodies.
bio:
Johanna is a lifelong dancer. She's the co-founder of the moving meditation practice, Earthance for Everyone. She's been dancing ecstatic for over a decade and contact for a few years. 
She likes to come back to basics in the sessions she facilitates. She has a gift for bridging worlds. She facilitates all kinds of things - like weddings and unions, learning music and meditation - and is influenced by her embodiment journey through connecting with country, meditation, yoga, dance, Kinesiology, Craniosacral Therapy and Feldenkrais.

details: How often do we let ourselves sink in and really be held by nature? And tune in, first thing in the morning, and connect with our nature? Join us for a meditative meander off the beaten track.
bio: Johanna was a force of nature behind Gather Australia, bringing people into the desert and the Kimberley to connect with Indigenous elders and return to reverence. She’s been through lore a couple of times. She is the author of the Circle of Life, an autobiographical story about connecting with your nature. She travelled around Australia as a kid, grew up in the country and has just moved back into the city, after spending the last decade in the bush.

workshop_name: Feeling Our Way Through : Anger & Fear as Collective Intelligence
details: We’ll explore how Anger and Fear, as collective intelligence, offer signals that shape conflict, participation and decision-making, helping build capacity to navigate change together.
bio:
Stacia is a researcher of radical human relating who is fed by challenging social norms. She is a writer, speaker, wisdom keeper, trainer, facilitator and world-bridger.

As a co-founder of The Art of Relating & The Reclaiming Anger Program, she facilitates safe and transformational spaces with individuals, groups and workplaces to explore what else is possible in human relating.

workshop_name: Resilience: 5 Tools for a Regulated Nervous System
details: Hands-on regulation lab: test 5 trauma-informed tools you can use when stress hits. Includes sensory nature walk + gentle seated/lying movements. No touch or deep sharing. Leave with your toolkit.
bio: From sales superstar to somatic trauma release work, Chu Wung is transitioning into something more aligned with his soul’s purpose. His approach is rooted in Somatic Experiencing principles and focuses on helping people meet stress and activation with more steadiness through gentle, practical nervous-system tools. He’s supported 60+ one-to-one somatic trauma release/regulation sessions and brings a grounded, calm presence to group spaces.

details: Devotional chanting of mantra in song with live music through singing together in a call and response format. We meet the resonance of our collective hearts to feel a true sense of belonging.
bio:
Paul has been facilitating and supporting kirtans for over 20 years - he started his journey with Indian Tabla, learning in Varanasi and musically has woven his way  through many and varied instruments. He sings and plays harmonium, guitar, 3 string, piano, tabla and melodica. 

His students and friends  often join the Kirtan group and have played many festivals including Renaissance, Confest, Lovefest, Yoga camp, as well as monthly events in Dandenong Ranges yoga studios, churches, houses and out in nature. 

The kirtan pieces Paul sings at each event are a combination of the traditional, well known and original creative compositions. All are sung with devotion and joy to the great mystery and in resonance with spirit and love.

Paul says that each time we sing together it offers us an opportunity to gently open our heart door to let our true soul expression come through.

details: For connection, healing, and dancefloor consciousness, there’s no better DJ than Jimmy Strat, a.k.a. James Stratford — Melbourne’s fastest rising techno artist.
bio: Jimmy Strat uses electronic music as a tool for connection and recovery, blending techno, house and psychedelic influences into sets that are emotional as well as physical. Open about the role DJing played in supporting his mental health, his approach centres honesty, presence and shared experience on the dancefloor. He is part of the Shibumi Records platform — supporting artists who bring meaning, vulnerability and intent into club culture.

details: All original music weaving live guitar with electronic textures and melodies into rhythm-driven soundscapes — a unique experience to groove to.
bio: Formally trained as a classical guitarist and driven by a passion for electronic music, Jay composes across genres, crafting all-original music that weaves live guitar with electronic textures and melodies into rhythm-driven soundscapes — a unique experience to groove to.

details: Using vocal techniques to warm up, and collaborative vocal improv to support you in connecting to your deep prayer for your life, we create groovy tunes together, inspired by whales, we sing you up!
bio:
Producer Victoria Whelan is an Creative Ideas Factory who Ignites Change-Makers!

Producing over 12 national festival in the United Kingdom, Victoria has worked with Susanne Vega, Deepak Chopra, Rising Appalachia, Charles Eisenstein, Deva Premal and Miten. Plus many more awesome speakers and artists who are beacons for the world.

Before that work she worked in the music industry, co-producing over 30 albums, plus music videos, documentaries, graphic design and many brand launches.

A ridiculous creative in her own right with the Seed Festival, Visual Artist and over 11 Albums, including SHE Nation #riseinlove

details: Oki-do is a Japanese approach to yoga. It is a playful embodied practice that encourages laughter, partner work, with both energetic & finishing with relaxed postures.
bio: Stev completed Hatha yoga teacher training in 2006 & was a student of the Oki-do school in Carlton. Stev has trained as a circus teacher, in theatre & composes music. Stev has worked as an entertainer for 30 years

details: “We can’t solve our problems with the same thinking that created them.” - Through games, music and embodied exercises, we’ll explore principles of creativity - Listen like a thief, Fail joyfully…
bio: Simon Oats is a storyteller, musician, performer, theatre-maker, Steiner teacher and creativity coach. He also works with nonprofit leaders and changemakers to develop powerful, story-driven presentations and campaigns.

details: Embodied epistemology is both a "multi-cognitive" and "meta-cognitive" physical practice that involves exploring a range of "information channels" within your experience.
bio: Alexander is a psychotherapist, game developer and researcher at Monash University.

workshop_name: Take action on the highest purpose of your Earth Walk
details: This workshop facilitates 1) a deep personal insight experienced through Mental Time Travel and 2) how this insight could be practically expressed in your life path and Earth Walk 🌞
bio: Ashwattha (aka Tom Paul Haynes) is a Futurist, Coach and Meditation Teacher who is passionate about supporting individuals and groups to make breakthrough toward a thriving future. He works on village, city and national scale transformations and has established a global charity to develop case-study project in Kampong Cham, Cambodia. This project invites innovators to create a visionary, open-source model of village development that has positive relationship to urban life. The aim is to share this breakthrough approach with the Global South to navigate the passing VUCA times (volatile, uncertain, chaotic and adverse).

workshop_name: Reclaiming the Sacredness of Rage - For Women
details: I will guide women to build the subtle energy of sacred rage and cultivate the frequency and energy from within. Cultivating the ancient medicine woman within who knows the wisdom of sacred rage.
bio: A Somatic Practitioner and Process-worker, Meg helps women build relationship with their authentic anger. She also helps humans with Unshaming and somatic process work to reclaim their felt sense and authenticity. Meg has studied with Maya Luna from the Deep Feminine Mystery school, process-work teacher David Bedrick from Sante Fe Institute of Shame based studies and as a Somatic Educator at the Somatic Institute for Women.

facilitator_name: Kate Laurie, Pete Coles, Ari Amala, Chloe Ann Francis
details: Together we will create a gentle ritual container for our individual and collective grief to be held, loved, expressed, witnessed, and revealed in their gifts to each other.
bio:
Ari, Kate, Pete and Chloe are all psychotherapists who deeply value the connective and transformative nature of collective grief spaces. We are inspired by the work of Francis Weller, Joanna Macy, Stephen Jenkinson and others, and believe that there is much beauty, wholeness and gratitude to be found in sharing our grief together.

Photo credit: Esayu Etsub

details: Across the continent now called Australia, ancient songlines carry ancestral memory as First Nations Elders, healers and artists navigate colonisation through enduring culture.

details: Australian premiere video screening followed by a held group discussion about redefining sisterhood, radical responsibility and reclaiming our true feminine power. Women only.
